paper.title_en: Chiral Superconductivity Indifferent to Parent Topology in the Square-Lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard Model
paper.abstract_en: We study a $π$-flux square-lattice $t$-$t'$ Hofstadter-Hubbard model proposed to be realizable in twisted moiré bilayers. By tuning $U$ and $t'$ at half filling, ground-state density-matrix renormalization group simulations (DMRG) and a parton analysis identify an integer quantum Hall (IQH) phase, a chiral spin liquid (CSL), and an antiferromagnet (AFM) in the phase diagram, while charge and spin fluctuations from finite-temperature determinant quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) suggest a closing charge gap but an open spin gap at the IQH-CSL boundary, consistent with the topological criticality expected there. This model therefore produces a phase diagram hosting weakly correlated band topology (IQH), intrinsic topological order (CSL), and conventional symmetry breaking (AFM) side by side. Upon doping any of these three parent phases, a single chiral topological superconductor with spin Chern number $C_s=-2$ occupies nearly the entire phase diagram. DMRG, DQMC, and weak-coupling perturbation theory agree on its pairing symmetry. This shows that doping the topological band of our model robustly induces the same paired state throughout the phase diagram regardless of the character of the underlying correlated half-filled state and its magnetic fluctuations, whether an IQH, a spin liquid or a weakly fluctuating AFM.
